summary: The note profiles two experimental sound artists, Alisa Tran in Auckland and Jaxon Keeler in London, who build immersive auditory environments that defy genre. It describes their work, their direct-to-audience distribution through Bandcamp and SoundCloud, and their live performances that turn venues into instruments. It argues they are challenging the traditional music industry's gatekeepers and categorizations.
one_line: Experimental sound artists Alisa Tran and Jaxon Keeler create immersive soundscapes and performances that challenge genre categories and the traditional music industry.
key_facts: Alisa Tran is a composer based in Auckland, New Zealand, known for intricate sound collages of ambient recordings, nature sounds, and synthesized textures.
Alisa Tran released the album "Whispers of the Wind" on October 17, 2023.
Jaxon Keeler has captivated audiences in London with found sounds and sonic manipulation since his debut on November 5, 2023.
Jaxon Keeler turns everyday noises like the hum of a refrigerator or the click of a keyboard into the basis of his aural landscapes.
Jaxon Keeler's most recent work is "Urban Symphony," which asks listeners to reconsider city noise as music.
The note says a new era in musical innovation began post-September 2023, building on the foundations laid by electronic music pioneers.
Tran and Keeler both use platforms like Bandcamp and SoundCloud, often releasing music on a "pay what you want" basis.
Direct artist-to-listener distribution circumvents gatekeepers such as record labels, radio programmers, and distributors.
Record labels, venues, and radio stations rely on genre categorizations, which are hard to apply to Tran's and Keeler's work.
Alisa Tran performed in December 2023 at Wellington's City Gallery, using the space's acoustics as part of the presentation.
Concertgoers described Tran's performances as "more like sound art installations than gigs."
Jaxon Keeler performed at London's Tate Modern on January 15, 2024, using sensors and AI to adapt the performance in real time to the audience's movements and reactions.
